title: Magnesium Sulfate Infusion in Preeclampsia
scenario: A 29-year-old client at 37 weeks gestation with severe preeclampsia is receiving a continuous IV magnesium sulfate infusion for seizure prophylaxis. The nurse monitors the client hourly.

questions.subject: Maternal-Newborn
questions.stem: Based on the flowsheet trend, which findings indicate the client is developing magnesium sulfate toxicity? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Loss of deep tendon reflexes, respiratory depression, a rising serum level above the 4-7 mg/dL therapeutic range, and declining urine output (which reduces magnesium excretion) are the hallmark signs of magnesium toxicity. A gradual fall in blood pressure is the intended therapeutic effect, not toxicity.

questions.subject: Maternal-Newborn
questions.stem: Given the 13:00 findings, what is the nurse's priority action?

options.text: Stop the magnesium sulfate infusion and notify the provider
Increase the magnesium sulfate infusion rate
Continue the infusion and recheck reflexes in one hour

questions.rationale: Respiratory depression, absent reflexes, and a serum level of 9.6 mg/dL signal dangerous toxicity, so the infusion must be stopped immediately and the provider notified; calcium gluconate is the antidote. Continuing or increasing the infusion would worsen the toxicity.
